questions.q: What is the main claim of the essay?
options: Founders should hire professional managers and step back from details
Scaling founders should use a distinct 'founder mode', not manager mode
Venture investors should take over daily management of startups
Airbnb's growth proves that Silicon Valley's hiring methods work
questions.explain: The essay says conventional advice amounts to manager mode, which hurt founders.

questions.q: What advice did Chesky receive that led to disastrous results?
options: Hire good people and give them room to do their jobs
Replace most of the founding team with experienced executives
Run the company like Google, with autonomous product teams
Delegate hiring entirely to the board and outside recruiters
questions.explain: The advice was 'hire good people and give them room to do their jobs.'

questions.q: Whose practices did Chesky partly study to find a better way?
options: Jeff Bezos at Amazon
John Sculley at Apple
Bill Gates at Microsoft
Steve Jobs at Apple
questions.explain: He studied how Steve Jobs ran Apple.

questions.q: What did Steve Jobs do that the author cites as unusual?
options: Ran an annual retreat only for the executives highest on the org chart
Hired only founders and let them run each product line independently
Banned all meetings with direct reports to keep the company startup-like
Ran an annual retreat for the 100 most important people, not the top of the org chart
questions.explain: The retreat included the 100 most important people, not the highest on the org chart.

questions.q: What does the author suggest about founders' bad experiences?
options: Advice fits professional managers, so founders feel gaslit
Managers are always right, so founders should defer to executives
Founder mode is already well documented in business school books
Founders were mistaken, since everyone around them disagreed
questions.explain: Advice assumed professional management, and founders felt gaslit by VCs and execs.
